parties:
Ali Akbar Khan ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Gurudas Mondal and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 17. Mr Jabbar has further argued that for not having complied with the provision of Order 7 rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure the plaintiff is not entitled to any declaratory decree in respect of an immovable property because the suit land is not specified with boundaries and other particulars. This plea was not taken by the defendant in the written statements nor any issue was framed to that effect nor any case was made out by adducing evidence and further that in this respect it has not been urged before the trial Court and the Appellate Court below that the suit land is unspecified and vague. It is contended for the first time before this Court that the provision of Order 7 rule 3 has not been complied with in claiming the land in the suit. The suit being one for declaration of tithe, no relief has been sought for confirmation of possession or recovery of khas possession. Mr Sk Razzak Ali has contend that in a declaratory decree no execution is necessary. Specification of the land by boundary is required or may be a legal requirement in case of execution of decree for recovery of khas possession or in a decree for confirmation of possession. The plaintiff needs only a declaration as to his entitlement over his share in the land. His contention in this regard appears to be sound and acceptable. but this point was not at all confounded by the plaintiff in the court below. In the 42 DLR''s case (Noor Mohammad Khan and others vs Government of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh and others; page 434) as has been cited by Mr Md Abdul Jabbar, maintainability of the suit was decided on the basis of the plaintiff''s possession and it was held that plaintiff having failed to prove his possession in the suit land simple suit for declaration of his title is barred. So far the specification according to Order 7 rule 3 is concerned the plaintiff has given in the schedule, name of the mouzas, Khatian numbers, plot numbers, the quantum of land as well as the specific share of the plaintiff. Although the boundary has not been given but the plaintiff will be able to manage his possession in his share according to his entitlement in the property. It is not the case that the other co-sharers are claiming that the plaintiff is possessing more land than his share. In view of the above facts and circumstances the provision as laid down under Order 7 rule 3 cannot strictly apply.
